title: fix(scripts): read changeset polarity in the clause that carries the verb, and read the schema-absent bucket
body:
Refs #9754 — this card outlives one PR. Its triage ruling names two items; this
carries both, and #9754 stays open.

`Clause-②: no` — an instrument's own precision, its pin, and one adjudication
reading. No published surface moves.

## 1. The false-positive source the instrument names on itself

**Re-taken, and written down as a rule rather than as a coordinate.**
`scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` still carries a section headed **"The
three limits that produce this instrument's false positives"**, and the second
of the three is still named **POLARITY BY KEYWORD** in the file's own capitals.
Both names are exactly as the card's triage ruling quotes them, and both are
what this PR is about.

⛔ The line numbers the dispatch carried are deliberately NOT restated here.
They did resolve when I re-took them against `c0b68d14d`, this branch's merge
base — but they point at lines **this diff rewrites**, so writing them into this
PR's prose would make them born false the moment it lands. That is the defect
class this card exists to treat, and per this repo's commandment #11 the cite
that travels with the thing is the heading text and the limit's name.

The limit, in its own words, is that polarity "is read from negation words in
the sentence", so `It has no mirror entry today, so ... S declares K` inverted
the verdict on a key the sentence asserts.

**The repair.** Polarity is a property of the CLAUSE that carries the
declaration verb. The sentence is cut at clause boundaries — `;` `:` parens,
dashes, `⇒`, and the coordinators/subordinators `and` `but` `so` `which`
`while` `because` … — negators are read only inside the clause carrying the
verb, and each key takes the polarity of the declaration clause it is written
in. Two legs make it a reading rather than a weakening:

- a negator-led fragment keeps its own negation, so `declares X and no Y` reads
  correctly on BOTH halves;
- a key resolved across a sentence boundary (the pronoun case) has no clause of
  its own and takes the sentence's first declaration clause — which is the
  clause its verb is in. That is the blindness pin's shape.

`keyHead` is extracted so polarity and `backtickedKeys` locate the same heads.

### What it measures

Instrument: `pnpm census:changeset-polarity`. All readings below are that
instrument's, at the ref named with them.

- At `c0b68d14d` (this branch's base, pre-repair): 134 candidate contradictions
  across 58 entries.
- At `4979243ea` (this branch's head, post-repair): 143 across 58.

Decomposed over the same two runs: 31 flags drop and 40 appear. The 31 are
polarity false positives cleared — present members that an unrelated negator had
turned into contradicted negative claims. The 40 are **not new defects**: every
one is a key whose polarity flipped negative to positive and which the face does
not declare, i.e. pre-existing WINDOW-PAIRING and key-extraction noise that the
sentence-wide negation had been suppressing **by accident**. Whether such a flag
appeared used to depend on an unrelated word elsewhere in the sentence; it no
longer does. Some of those 40 are real candidates the old reading was hiding —
one example, judged by eye and not adjudicated, is an entry claiming a widget
face inherits a key through an `Omit` of a `Partial` of the spec-side type that the census reads
as absent.

⚠️ So this repair does **not** lower the count, and the count was never the
measure. Reported this way on purpose: a bare "134 → 143" carries the defect
this card is about.

### The blindness fixture — before and after

Run against the pre-repair text of the site that motivated #9727, carried in
`01-pronoun-pre-repair.md`:

| | flags | keys | reached across a sentence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| at `c0b68d14d` | 4 | `allowCollapse` `cardTitle` `columns` `titleField` | all |
| at `4979243ea` | 4 | `allowCollapse` `cardTitle` `columns` `titleField` | all |

Byte-identical: exactly the four keys #9713 adjudicated, every one still reached
across a sentence boundary, all negative, all on the surviving face. The
instrument was sharpened, not blunted.

### The pin, and proof it can fail

Pin 8 lands in `scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` against a
new fixture entry carrying all three shapes in one changeset, so both legs are
pinned against one reading: the false positive must go, AND a negator that does
scope the verb must still read negative. The fixture discriminates — the
pre-repair instrument reads four flags on it, two of them false; this one reads
the two denials and neither assertion.

Every pin was shown red. Three ablations, each mutated on disk with the
injection and the deletion counted before the run, each restored by
`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and the restore proven by blob hash equal to
HEAD's with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| ablation | mutation | pins red |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | the verdict ignores the per-key reading | 2 |
| A2 | clause cutting disabled — one clause is the whole sentence | 4 |
| A3 | `polarityOf` never reads negation | 5, including the #9727 blindness pin |

Union over the three: all six of pin 8's tests, plus two of pin 1's. A3 reddening
the blindness pin is the no-trade evidence — the guard against buying precision
with false negatives is itself live.

⛔ I did not attack the other two named sources. I measured what one of them
would do and stopped: bounding the declaration verb's reach to its own clause —
the key half of WINDOW PAIRING — takes the same instrument from 134 candidates
across 58 entries at `c0b68d14d` to 43 across 30, dropping 107 flags that nobody
has adjudicated. That is the largest source and it needs its own card and its own
adjudication, not a side effect of this one. The measurement is in my hand-back.

## 2. A first adjudication reading of the schema-absent bucket

⛔ Nothing in this bucket was swept, repaired or touched. This is a reading.

**How it was drawn — reproducibly, and it is a census rather than a sample.**
`pnpm census:changeset-polarity --json` at `4979243ea` reports 61 matched
assertions naming a schema symbol this tree does not declare, over 35 distinct
symbols (unchanged by this PR: the same instrument reads 61 at `c0b68d14d`). All
35 were classified mechanically, so there is no sampling error to report: for
each symbol, grep for a DECLARATION of it (`interface|type|class|const X`) in
(a) the census corpus `packages/types/src`, (b) the rest of this repo's
`packages`/`apps`/`e2e` sources, (c) the installed `@objectstack` dependencies.

**The reading.**

| kind | assertions | share | symbols | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| declared and alive in `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0`, outside the census corpus | 57 | 93% | 31 | high — each located at a named file in the installed dependency |
| declared in this repo outside `packages/types/src` | 1 | 2% | 1 (`LineItemsPanelSchema`, in `packages/plugin-form`) | high — same method |
| retired: the corpus directory names it only in a retirement comment | 3 | 5% | 3 (`KanbanSchema`, `BlockSchema`, `BlockInstanceSchema`) | high on the location, ⛔ NOT adjudicated as rot |

**What that says.** The schema-absent bucket is overwhelmingly not a defect list
and not a rot list — it is a measurement of the census's own corpus boundary.
The census resolves membership against `packages/types/src`; a changeset that
names a protocol symbol is naming something that lives in `@objectstack/spec`,
where the census cannot see it. 93% of the bucket is that, and none of it is
dispatchable as a repair.

**The residue, and where it stops.** Three assertions name a symbol that is
genuinely undeclared anywhere readable, each mentioned inside
`packages/types/src` only in a comment recording its retirement:

- `KanbanSchema` (one assertion) reaches the census through a joined TABLE ROW
  in a dated history ledger, whose own text says the arm was retired. Reading it
  as a live present-tense claim is a segmentation artifact, not a rot.
- `BlockSchema` / `BlockInstanceSchema` (two assertions, one sentence) is a
  genuine present-tense claim about symbols this tree has since retired — a
  ROTTED candidate.

⚠️ **裁决必须先于触碰**, so that is where this reading stops. ROTTED and BORN
FALSE take opposite repairs and BORN FALSE is only decidable at the sentence's
own write-time ref; this checkout is shallow (`git rev-parse
--is-shallow-repository` answers true), so establishing either verdict costs a
deepen plus a history read per site. ⛔ Not done here, and ⛔ nothing repaired.

## Tests

All at `4979243ea`, exit codes captured to a file before any pipe.

- `npx vitest run --project unit scripts/__tests__/changeset-polarity-census.test.ts` — 29 passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm type-check:scripts` — exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0; its own verdict line:
  "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range,
  so no changeset is owed."
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — exit 0.
- Derived from the four changed paths: `check:control-bytes`,
  `check:new-line-citations`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`,
  `check:test-path-roots`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:changeset-claims`,
  `check:pending-changeset-literals` — all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four changed paths — exit 0,
  "NOT GOVERNED".
- Lint: `lint:root` is the population that governs `scripts/**`, and it was run
  whole rather than narrowed — 377 files by eslint's own `--format json` count,
  exit 0, 0 errors and 32 pre-existing warnings. The packages/apps/examples/docs
  populations were not run: this diff touches no package source, and
  `eslint.config.js` configures no type-aware linting (no `project` /
  `projectService`), so it cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.
- Full workspace build (`turbo run build --filter=!@object-ui/site`) — 43 tasks
  successful, exit 0. Run for the changeset measurement below.

### Changeset grade — measured from that build, with both controls on one corpus

The changeset carries empty frontmatter. The corpus is every file on disk under
all 39 release packages' `files[]` after the build above: 7734 files.

| probe | role | files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ObjectKanbanSchema` | lit control | 26 |
| `retirementTombstone` | lit control | 34 |
| a token that cannot occur | absent control | 0 |
| `readPolarity` | this diff | 0 |
| `clauseTexts` | this diff | 0 |
| `CLAUSE_BREAK` | this diff | 0 |
| `07-polarity-clause-scope` | this diff | 0 |

Lit controls light and the absent control is dark on the same corpus, so the
zeros are measurements. Nothing this PR changes is published.

## Acceptance notes

- `e2e/live/global-setup.ts` reports one `no-console` error under
  `eslint --no-inline-config`, because that flag disables a legitimate
  `eslint-disable-next-line` the file carries. Pre-existing, untouched by this
  branch, and green under the repo's own `lint:root`. Noted, not filed.
- The 40 newly-surfaced flags are pre-existing noise from the two sources this PR
  does not attack, now reported consistently instead of accidentally. Material
  for whoever takes WINDOW PAIRING; the measurement is in my hand-back.
